finding.claim: t is the string result of typeof, so t === null is never true; null therefore falls through to value.buffer which throws TypeError instead of returning true.
finding.title: isJSONSerializable crashes on null due to typeof comparison

verifier.reason: Confirmed at utils.ts:21-32: t is the string from typeof, so t === null at utils.ts:22 is never true, typeof null is "object" so it passes utils.ts:25, Array.isArray(null) is false, and utils.ts:31 then dereferences null.buffer throwing a TypeError.

finding.claim: Truthiness test on body skips valid falsy JSON bodies like 0, "" and false, so they miss stringify and content-type handling.
finding.title: Falsy request bodies are skipped by truthiness check

verifier.reason: The guard at fetch.ts:130 uses truthiness on context.options.body, so 0 and false skip the block at fetch.ts:131-153 that stringifies and sets application/json headers, even though utils.ts:22 explicitly treats number and boolean values as JSON-serializable.

finding.claim: Prefix test without slash boundary treats /apiary as already based on /api and returns it unchanged instead of joining to /api/apiary.
finding.title: withBase prefix check lacks path-boundary

verifier.reason: Confirmed: at utils.url.ts:45-48, _base is '/api' for base '/api' and '/apiary'.startsWith('/api') is true, so withBase returns '/apiary' unchanged and never reaches joinURL at utils.url.ts:50 which would produce '/api/apiary'.

finding.claim: Array values are appended without deleting existing params while scalar values use set, so retrying withQuery on a URL with existing query leaves stale values.
finding.title: withQuery array branch does not replace existing params

verifier.reason: The code at utils.url.ts:86 parses existing query params, then utils.url.ts:92-97 appends array items without deleting the key while scalar values use set to replace it, so pre-existing values remain alongside new array values.
